root_idea.summary: The root denotes the opposite of blame: praise directed toward a praiseworthy quality, action, or object.
root_idea.development: Its lexical range develops from praising or recognizing praiseworthiness to expressions for being praised, praising repeatedly, praiseworthy qualities, and the state or result of being commendable. Some fire-related terms in the transmitted lexicon are treated as transposed forms rather than part of this root principle.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested passive Form I verb.
Distinct Quran-attested adjective and nominal epithet.

senses.definition: To be praised, eulogized, or commended.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrence is the passive imperfect يُحْمَدُ, ‘they be praised’; the active lexical counterpart is to praise or commend.
The Quranic form is plural, حَامِدُونَ; in the cited construction the praise is directed to God.

senses.definition: Praised or praiseworthy; possessing qualities for which praise is due.
senses.usage_conditions: It is frequently an epithet of God, including the sense of one who is praiseworthy in every case.

In the Quranic expression إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ, the lexical explanation allows حَمِيدٌ to be understood in the active sense الحامد, as well as in the passive or evaluative sense ‘praised, praiseworthy’.

In Quranic formulas it is especially praise directed to God. The lexical distinction supplied for this noun makes it narrower than generic مدح and broader than شكر: it is not restricted to gratitude for a received benefit. With بِحَمْدِكَ and related constructions, it can mean praising You or ‘praise be to You’.
This is the passive-participial form of the root and may describe one who is praised or an object deserving praise.

senses.definition: The praised station; a station in which its occupant is praised by all creatures, or the station of intercession.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized interpretation belongs to the Quranic expression المَقَامُ المَحْمُودُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To praise, eulogize, commend, or speak well of someone or something; to mention it with approval.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may take عَلَى for the matter for which someone is praised. Praise may express admiration, magnification, or honoring, together with humility in the person offering it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approve of a matter for someone; with حَمِدَ إِلَيْهِ, to approve it for someone and enjoin or recommend it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional evaluative construction, also used of approving a neighbor, place, or other circumstance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recompense or requite someone; to give or pay someone his due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Classical use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be angry with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is associated with the construction حَمِدَ عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To praise God much, repeatedly, or time after time; to declare His praises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II is intensive or iterative relative to حَمِدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become praiseworthy or commendable; to do or say what deserves praise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person, action, affair, or result that comes into a praiseworthy state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find or judge someone or something praiseworthy, commendable, approved, or suitable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person, action, course of conduct, belief, land, or place; the meaning is evaluative rather than a restriction to any one object class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or make a show of praise, or to present oneself as praiseworthy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical attribution also gives ‘to praise oneself’; the transmitted evidence treats this as a reported usage rather than an undisputed definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reproach someone for a favor bestowed, or to recount one’s gifts or actions to that person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This construction is given as synonymous with اِمْتَنَّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To praise or commend one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal Form VI may also describe people mutually praising a thing, such as herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of heat, to burn fiercely or become vehement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a transposed form of اِحْتَدَمَ, not as the ordinary praise branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand praise; in a transmitted expression, to demand that creatures praise God for His beneficence and bounty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source text is uncertain: it transmits an imperative reading but proposes reading اِسْتَحْمَدَ اللَّهُ, ‘God demanded praise’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The young one of the bird called قَطًا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate lexical item from حَمْدٌ ‘praise’ despite the identical consonantal spelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of a flaming or blazing fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted lexicographic explanation treats it as a transposed form related to حَدَمَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The utmost of one’s power or ability; figuratively, one’s utmost praiseworthy action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is followed by the action that represents the limit of one’s ability or praiseworthy conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who praises much, frequently, or extravagantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet can be used specifically of one who praises God repeatedly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the proverb, repetition is more deserving of praise or brings more praise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is explained through the approval implied by returning to something after experience of it, or through the greater praise attached to repeating a good action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A praiseworthy or approvable quality, action, or cause of praise; a thing for which one is praised or approved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural مَحَامِدُ also means forms or instances of praise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More praiseworthy; as a personal name, Aḥmad, one characterized as more praiseworthy than others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Quran-focused explanation connects the name Aḥmad with both the Prophet’s name and his praiseworthy qualities, and with being more praiseworthy than those before him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One praised much, repeatedly, or time after time; one endowed with many praiseworthy qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: As a proper name, the form retains an allusive connection with repeated or abundant praise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a dwelling or place, praised, approved, convenient, or suitable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a transferred Classical use applied to a place where one alights, sojourns, or abides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a day, intensely or vehemently hot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This derived adjective is associated with the transposed heat sense of اِحْتَمَدَ.

cautions: حَمِيدٌ in 11:73 is explicitly open to both the passive/evaluative sense ‘praised, praiseworthy’ and the active sense ‘praising’.
The Form X evidence is textually uncertain: the transmitted imperative and the proposed reading اِسْتَحْمَدَ اللَّهُ yield different grammatical interpretations.
Fire-related entries such as حَمَدَةٌ and اِحْتَمَدَ are lexically reported as transpositions and should not be used to define the core praise meaning of the root.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Form X entry lane-unit:Hmd:15593:g1:main preserves a disputed reading: the source transmits a command to demand praise but proposes that the text should instead mean ‘God demanded praise of His creatures’.
